analysisMethod: Invented sample for trying the source fix flow. It is not a Coverity scan or a native Coverity export, and it describes the made-up 'shop' Java project of the demos. Issue IDs are local fixture identifiers, not vendor CIDs.
description: Two source findings of a small made-up Java project, for testing NATS-triggered remediation. Paths are relative to projectPath.

issues.title: User name is concatenated into a SQL query

relatedLocations.role: The name comes from the request and is passed to findUser

issues.evidence: Db.findUser builds the query text with the name argument and hands it to driver.query.
dataFlow: A request supplies a user name.
Shop passes it to Db.findUser unchanged.
Db.findUser concatenates it into the SQL text.
issues.impact: A crafted name can change the query and read other rows.
preconditions: A caller can choose the name.
issues.limitations: Static finding; no exploit was run.
remediation: Use a parameterized query or a prepared statement.
verification: Add a test with a name that contains a quote and a SQL comment.

issues.title: Database password is compiled into the class
issues.evidence: Db.connect passes a string literal as the password to the driver.
dataFlow: The literal is part of the compiled class.
Db.connect hands it to the driver on every connection.
issues.impact: Anyone with the source or the compiled class knows the password; it also stays in the version history.
preconditions: The class or the source is readable by someone who should not know the password.
issues.limitations: The old password in the history must be rotated; a code change cannot remove it.
remediation: Read the password from the environment (DB_PASSWORD) and fail clearly when it is missing.
Tell the owner to rotate the old password.
verification: Add a test that sets and clears the variable.
